source.title: Efficient Training-Free Multi-Token Prediction via Embedding-Space Probing
source.authors: Raghavv Goel; Mukul Gagrani; Min-Gu Lee; Christopher Lott

record.tranche_reason: The study tests future-token prediction with embedding-space mask-token probes and verification, a different method from single-hidden-state readouts or rhyme-ending interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper injects synthetic mask embeddings and measures speculative-token acceptance, hidden-state similarity, and performance on several task types. It does not test rhyme-word planning or whether swapping a candidate rhyme ending causally changes intervening verse. Its citations to Future Lens and Do language models plan ahead are background, not results from those studies.
record.test_reason: ESP is a speculative-decoding method. It relies on latent future-token predictability as a tool and reports its own performance: acceptance length and speedup against PLD, STAND, LADE and EAGLE3, plus ablations of its design. Predictions come from synthetic mask embeddings appended to the input, not from an ordinary hidden state. No rhyme planning, pre-caching test or causal intervention is reported. Its numbers measure the method's efficiency, not whether any claim version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that mask-token probing of frozen LLMs gives lossless multi-token speculative decoding that beats training-free baselines; even one mask token helps. They attribute this to late-layer alignment of mask and true-token states and leave open how that information arises. They also report that open-ended tasks favour wider trees and closed-ended tasks deeper trees.
record.recipe_differences: ESP inserts dynamically initialized embedding-space mask tokens and evaluates their future-token proposals by speculative verification. It does not use rhyme prompts, ordinary hidden-state decoding as its main method, or a causal intervention that swaps a future ending.
record.method_sensitivity: Acceptance varies with model, block complexity, task, number of mask tokens, mask initialization, tree branching/pruning, and mask-token update rate. The paper reports one-mask versus multi-mask differences by task and says prompt-mean initialization performs best among tested initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen LLaMA3 and Qwen3 models with prompt-mean mask embeddings appended propose future tokens that pass exact-match verification. Average τ is about 1.56–1.74 including the bonus token (Table 1). Gains shrink beyond two masks (1.65/1.63/1.51 for LLaMA3.2-3B at BC=60). Accepted mask tokens show higher late-layer similarity to the true-token state (~0.45 vs ~0.35).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frozen next-token LLMs can be elicited, via synthetic mask-token inputs, to predict tokens 2–3 positions ahead with modest accuracy that declines with depth.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026)
record.problems: The study uses injected mask embeddings and a speculative-decoding procedure, so results do not establish that natural-position hidden states pre-cache future-useful features. Acceptance lengths are averages without reported uncertainty. The hidden-state similarity result is correlational. No rhyme-ending intervention is performed.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted detailed per-task plot values in Figures 4, 5 and 8 where the text provides no exact values, and omitted implementation/algorithm ablations such as initialization, update rate, pruning, and branch-search comparisons; these evaluate ESP design choices rather than separately isolating the claim's core hidden-state or causal-planning mechanisms.

untested.parts: All: no verse, rhyme candidates or interventions.
Decodability of future tokens from a single natural hidden state. Predictions here come from extra mask-token inputs processed by the model.
All: no test separating pre-caching from breadcrumbs. It is cited only as background.
All: no rhyme planning, attribution graphs or probes for a planning mechanism.
All: no internal look-ahead mechanism in reasoning, chess or Sokoban.
Horizon or heuristic explanations of natural plans. The mask-count ablations concern the method's design.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V2/V5/V6 labels are withdrawn. The paper is a method paper whose rows are its own performance and ablations; it cites Future Lens and Wu et al. only as rationale. Its theoretical lemma links cosine similarity to top-K inclusion and is not evidence on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse prompts, candidate rhyme-word readouts, or intervention changing an ending to test its effect on the line.

The study tests predictions elicited at injected mask-token positions, not whether an ordinary hidden state at an earlier natural-token position contains the same information; it does not isolate arbitrary long horizons from one state.
No test distinguishes features computed for later-position usefulness from incidental next-token prediction features, and no pre-caching/breadcrumbs intervention.
It uses smaller LLaMA and Qwen models, but does not test rhyme planning or use open attribution-graph or probing tools to identify that mechanism.
It reports results on SpecBench tasks including math/reasoning and uses LLaMA3 and Qwen3 models, but does not test chess or Sokoban, and does not isolate a general multi-step-reasoning mechanism.
It tests diminishing predictive performance with more mask tokens and reports task/configuration differences. It does not establish that local next-token features or heuristics explain the results.

relation.reason: Section 5 explicitly uses Future Lens single-state decodability as rationale for ESP. Its experiments evaluate mask-token proposals rather than independently testing that finding.

tranche.reason: ESP uses future-token predictability for speculative decoding and evaluates its own performance and design. Injected mask positions and acceptance lengths do not test decodability several positions ahead from a single hidden state.

source_check.notes: The cosine values are explicitly stated in Section 3.2, not merely estimated from Figure 2. Acceptance lengths are method-performance results; Table 3 confounds mask count with branch width, and Table 9 increases mask count and budget together.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ESP mask-token probing on SpecBench, across the four evaluated models and block complexities 30 and 60
reader_labels.reason: All reported mean acceptance lengths exceed 1; the study reports accepted speculative tokens after verification (r1–r8). This supports some future-token predictability under the probing setup, not a long horizon from one ordinary hidden state.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Mask/true-token cosine similarity is higher for accepted than rejected predictions, but the reported comparison is correlational and does not test ordinary-position states or a causal change to intermediate text (r9–r10).

reader_labels.reason: The paper reports accepted future-token predictions across model families and a benchmark covering multiple tasks, with additional math/reasoning results (r1–r8, r11–r12).
